Jeff

notes.title: WE'RE A-FIRIN' OUR LAYZAH!!
notes.content:
Weekly Dev Update #75
Week of August 29, 2022

This week at Mutant, we’re a-firin’ our layzah! 

Zach’s in full monster mode, ramping up our Kaiju fight systems and getting us ready to really show off what’s going to make Kaiju Fishing the most epic fishing experience you’ll ever have.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/f188d538dd6db9840e2d1fae61beca1f2b6595e2.gif[/img]

[h3]KAIJU FISHING BOSS FIGHTS[/h3]
We’ve gone over the storyboards for the boss fight in previous weeklies and we’ve shown you the big guy in action in our trailers, but now it’s time to put it all together. 

To recap: Kaiju Fishing boss fights are going to be broken into a few stages, with mechanics from our usual small and medium fishing as well as the need to use some new and wild tools.
[olist]
[*] You gotta get its attention. This will be done with an ancient Summoning Bell (which you’ll charge up by catching other fish). Charging the bell for each area proves your angler skill and proves you’re ready to face the Kaiju. Ring the bell in the arena to call the boss to you.
[*] Hooking the monster. Easier said than done. This will be different from our usual fishing; it’d be a bit odd to see a Godzilla-sized creature nibble at a normal line, so instead you’ll need to get close and shoot your special plunger-fish at certain points on its body. The plunger fish is a sweet and magical little creature that Sarah concepted which will act as a sort of leech, “cleansing” the monster of the dark energy in it as you fight. (Maybe we'll show that little guy off next week!)
[*] The Kaiju won't be the biggest fan of you at this point. In fact, it’s gonna want to swat you like a mosquito. Now is when you need to dodge and dodge well. We’ve got a plethora of attacks for each monster - the one we showed off earlier in the summer was the tail slap but there are a few more tricks up our sleeve just for this fight.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/5b0ce2a9331ac974de159124c21289ab57b76273.jpg[/img]
[*] Keep going! If the monster breaks free, hook it again. If you get hit, learn from it and dodge the next. The boss fight itself is still being tuned, but we’re targeting three-ish major phases rotating through the different attacks we’ve got set up for you. Drain all the darkness from the mighty beast and you’ll be the victor.
[/olist]
And that’s it! Easy, right? (Not really, don’t get hit too many times or you’ll have to restart the fight.)

[h3]HYPER BEAMS ARE FUN[/h3]
So I figured now is a good time to show you another sneak preview of one of our attacks - and this is one I hold very near and dear to my heart… the inspiration should be obvious!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/168052f296cb8bb06ec5ccb3605a37c949113b33.gif[/img]

Zach did an amazing job with the effect and we all can’t wait to keep pushing our visual effects, plus Sarah’s got the new Kaiju model just about ready to go… oh yeah, it’s all coming together. I hope you’re as excited about this as I am because I am so desperately looking forward to each playtest.

And this is where I’ll leave another reminder that we have a Discord… and it’s a Discord where playtests can and will happen… and you, yes you, will be able to play Kaiju fights early when we’re ready to test the fight… I’m just sayin’.

notes.title: "ICE" TO BE BACK
notes.content:
Weekly Dev Update #73
Week of May 30th, 2022

This week at Mutant, did ya miss us? We missed you. 

I’m back after a too-long “break.” Took some time off to move to a new apartment, which ended up a lot more chaotic and exhausting (and expensive) than I wanted it to be. It was a long week of calling a million apartment listings and then an even longer weekend of driving hundreds of miles in the moving truck and lifting heavy things on both sides of the trip. My back, arms, legs, and brain are all tired… and possibly injured.

But hey! The team has been kicking butt even in my absence, so let’s catch up with some of their progress. We’ve got art and waterfall things to dive into so let’s get started. 

[h3]ICE, ICE, BABY[/h3]
[i]Have I used that title before? Maybe. Is that gonna stop me from using it now? No.[/i]

We’re ramping up to get our ice realm underway and while we’re nailing down plans for the environment, Sarah’s been touching up the designs for our ice fish. Remember, each region has unique fish for you to catch and collect. Let’s take a peek!

First up, this bulbous-brained small fry.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/3d8c1acf0e56a1bc0e0596929db19543fe7a129d.jpg[/img]

Next, a shy little crustacean. He just wants a friend. Or two.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/93abb61a69ec0cb669cc956e938d1376cfd740a1.jpg[/img]

Now we get up to the mediums, like this hard-scaled, six-eyed fish with… ice spikes? God that’s cool. How does she come up with these?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/3bcecf04f6e6314825d670c73049a588f2e3587f.jpg[/img]

And finally, a wizened turtle. Loving the beard, bro!  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/80bfdfb380b78ed56b588dc28c8a2b2377308d1f.jpg[/img]

[h3]THE WATERFALL PARADOX[/h3]
“To put loot behind the waterfall… or to not put loot behind the waterfall?” - Shakespeare, probably.

For millennia, game designers have struggled with the impossible question of whether to be predictable and put a treasure behind a waterfall or leave it empty. Gamers have longer wondered why calling something predictable has led to a shortage of loot hidden behind said waterfalls. The discussion is a circle. The debate wages on and always will, but for us the answer is… play the game and find out. [i]There will probably be some fish in those caves at the very least…[/i]

We are excited to include waterfalls around our different areas either way. Zach did some research into the viability and have some early proof-of-concept concepts that I just couldn’t wait to share. Check it out!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/3679e147721af11a2a5cf93945171c689f603824.gif[/img]

[h3]FOLLOW US FOR MORE[/h3]
That’s all we got for ya this week. I’m glad to be back. My wife and I are still living out of boxes because, well, does anyone ever really unpack all of the things you move with? (If you say yes, I'm just gonna assume you're a liar.) Anyways. I’m ready to get back to it and eager to share all the fun new things with all of you. We have a busy summer planned, so stay tuned!

notes.title: ROGUE JAM - IGN, WTF, AND OTHER ACRONYMS
notes.content:
Weekly Dev Update #72
Week of May 2nd, 2022

This week at Mutant, we’ve gone ROGUE (JAM)! We can finally talk about all it.

A while back, we submitted Kaiju Fishing for the Rogue Jam competition and we successfully made it to the final round of their “WTF” category. Judges included big names like beloved ex Nintendo of America President Reggie and we went up against some other awesome Indie games. The other finalists were all really cool, so we had fun going up against them and seeing what they have in store. 

We can’t link directly to it here, but you can find it on the IGN Youtube page titled ‘WTF Games Compete for $100K Prize | Rogue Jam Ep. 3.’ It aired on Monday, so we hope you’ll give it a watch! 

It was an honor to be a finalist in our group and to be featured in this show. Big thanks to IGN and Rogue for hosting! And if you stop by our Twitter or the Youtube videos, show some love to Zach for being our spokesperson. He represented us excellently so a big thanks to him for all of his effort.

[i]I won’t spoil the result at the top here in case you want to watch the episode and be surprised, but I’ll talk about the result at the end of this post so watch the episode before you finish reading this update if you want to be spoiler-free! (It'll be right below the image in this so uh, you've been warned.)[/i]

[h3]BRR, AN ICY STORE PAGE UPDATE[/h3]
In preparation for the episode, we wanted to spruce up our store page and do some “spring cleaning” in the process. We’ve updated the description to better fit our different features and story, and we’ve added some new screenshots highlighting the different environments that you’ll find in Kaiju Fishing.

notes.title: LET. ME. UPDATE. THE. CLAMPJAW!
notes.content:
Weekly Dev Update #70
Week of March 21, 2022

This week at Mutant, let’s talk about fishing as “combat” and look at a sneak peak of an update heading directly to the Kaiju Fishing Demo.

[h3]FISHING AS COMBAT[/h3]
We’ve spent a lot of time trying to make the fishing feel alive and appropriately difficult but we know we can push this boundary further. We want fishing to act as our game’s “combat” system and to reach that goal, there are a couple of angles we want to tackle.

Our current system primarily focuses on “reaction” moves. The fish does a move and you react, either with a button press/hold or a movement counter. To us, this was a natural starting point as fishing has a lot of reactionary actions in real life. But in our fantasy adventure game, we can do more! We’ve had ideas to give players more abilities and tools in the back pocket for a while now and this shift in philosophy is going to give us the room to play with those. 

These abilities are going to start at the larger end, at least from a development perspective, but we want to be able to apply these actions all the way down to small fish. One idea that we’re bringing back from an old, old version of this project is a dodge… so we’ll let you imagine how we might apply that.

We also want to double back to our fish AI, in a few ways. We want them to feel more alive and give them more responses to your actions too. If you want them to go somewhere, they should counter you. If you throw an attack at them, they should be able to dodge or resist.

And that’s all you get for now… we’ll share more as we get further along. Let’s get to the immediate Demo stuff!

[h3]LET. ME. UPDATE. THE. CLAMPJAW!!![/h3]
“Please let me update this fish!” Our artist is a driven and proud person and while we always think her creations are wonderful, she is determined to keep her work evolving. The Clampjaw is a classic example of this. This medium fish was one of the first designs we approved and one of the first she modeled for the game. It’s also been one of the only medium fish in the Demo, so it’s the one we look at most often while testing.

In her eyes, this makes the Clampjaw a prime candidate for “I can make it better now.” And y’know what? We believe her. We’ve finally made space in our schedule and she leapt at the chance! So here he is: the updated Clampjaw.

Don’t let Kaiju Fishing be the last stop on your indie browsing adventure, make sure to check out as many of the cool projects as you can! And remember to Wishlist and follow the ones you like!

You can also follow @MutantStudios on Twitter, join our Discord, and join our mailing list to see more behind-the-scenes work on all of our projects. Thank you for your support!

[h3]DEMO UPDATE[/h3]
[b]Kaiju Fishing Patch Notes (August 2021)[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/1c2560b5bce0b7355d707e480307b8daecd1dce3.jpg[/img]
Timed perfectly with this event, we just launched a significant patch to the Kaiju Fishing Steam Demo! There’s new fish and new mechanics, so there’s something here for you whether you’re new or returning! This will mostly cover the same stuff that we linked in our Patch Notes for the current build, but we wanted to include the full list here too so you just can't miss em! You can download and play the Kaiju Fishing Demo RIGHT NOW! Check it out!

We have a lot of cover in this Demo update, so let’s dive right in.

[b]Gameplay[/b]
Medium Fish[list]
[*] Medium Fish are finally here! Two different species have been spotted in the enclosed Demo area and are now available to find and catch. Keep your eyes peeled for ‘em - but they’re pretty hard to miss!
[*] Medium Fishing is a new activity altogether, so get ready for a ride.
[*] New tutorials for Medium Fishing added.
[/list][i]And keep in mind that Medium Fishing isn’t our final escalation. We have Large and the much anticipated Kaiju lurking for the full release. You might even spot one past the safety of the rocks...[/i]

Fishing
[list]
[*] Added a new "Strike" system when fishing. Missing QTEs adds a strike and if you hit the limit the line will break (think 'Striking Out' in baseball). The limit is 3 for all of the fish in the Demo, but there will be a range of Strike Limits in the full release. You will also be able to increase this with the proper bait and items in the full game.
[*] Fish attacks have had their tension increases lowered across the board with most attacks focused on dealing Strike damage.
[*] Reeling now increases tension slightly faster.
[*] Removed movement-based/control-stick "QTEs" and accompanying UI alerts. We didn't like the game-feel of them (including how we were showing feedback for success/failure of the action), especially combined with Strikes. You can still move the rod to steer the fish where you'd like and you should; if the fish gets too far to the side your tension will increase more. Fish will also continue to do the "moves" like zig-zag but with less emphasis on directly impacting tension.
[*] Increased "second chance" window. This is when you've hit the breaking point of tension, if you stop reeling quickly you can save the catch.
[*] Cancelling a cast now requires a button/key hold instead of one press. This is to prevent accidental cancelations. 
[*] Reeling now moves fish more directly to the boat's catch areas. This should prevent fish from becoming caught underneath the boat when nearing a catch.
[/list]
[b]Exploration[/b]
Open Sail Movement[list]
[*] Speed increased from 15 to 35
[*] Turn speed increased from 0.8 to 1.3
[*] Time to Full Speed increased from 1.3 to 2 seconds
[*] Open Sail Camera Adjusted (Orbit ranges increased to be further back and higher up)
[*] Open Sail Camera FOV decreased
[/list]
Closed Sail Movement (Cruising)[list]
[*] Speed increased from 5 to 15
[*] Turn power increased from .5 to 1
[*] Time to full speed decreased from 2.5 to 1.2
[/list]
Environment[list]
[*] Fish spawns have been adjusted to increase the need to roam. Each zone now only has one type of fish. We want you to explore and find new schools, rather than just hit up the same spot over and over. This will be a part of more complex systems in the full release as we add in baits and other tools.
[*] Updated the ocean color to give a better sense of depth. We are moving away from having too many shallow areas, so the ocean will be getting darker.
[*] Updates to splash effects during fishing.
[/list]
[b]Menus and General Systems[/b]
Controls[list]
[*] Mouse and Keyboard support has been added and tuned. Hopefully this opens up the game to more players who might not have controllers at home! Big thanks to everyone who tested this early over on Itch and on our Discord <3
[*] Spyglass feature disabled - for now. It wasn’t a priority for us to update here and we feel it isn’t quite polished enough to keep around. It’ll return with new uses later!
[/list]
Quest[list]
[*] We've expanded the quest from our shopkeeper to include the Medium Fish and changed some of the dialogue. Part of this was switching ourselves over to a new dialogue manager, so while it looks the same the guts are different and it'll be easier for us to make content as we go. We aren't planning any more major quest updates in the Demo build as we'll be focusing that attention on the full release, but we'll keep you posted.
[*] Our shopkeeper also has a swanky new ride. For now, he’s parked it by his little island but he’ll be hittin’ the seas in the full release!
[/list]
Tutorial[list]
[*] We've done away with our old panels and have moved to more context-based panels. These are meant to give you the information you need immediately before you engage in a new mechanic and should make it all a little easier to digest. 
[*] If you want to see the Tutorials again, a toggle is available in the Settings Menu in the Gameplay section.
[/list]
UI Updates[list]
[*] Menus, Alerts, Dialogue Boxes, and Pop-Ups have all been updated to a new style of art.
[/list]
[b]Bug Fixes[/b][list]
[*] Fixes to catching fish, including menus and issues with releasing fish.
[*] Fixes to fishing mechanics, including lingering QTEs and weird interactions.
[*] Fixes to camera transitions and camera rotations.
[*] Fixes to controller rumble, which could continue after certain actions.
[*] Fixes to Quest tracking.
[*] Fixes to menu navigation.
[*] Fixes to environment collisions that could cause the boat to get stuck.
[/list]

Whew, I think that's everything. There might be some additional bug fixes that I didn't cover directly, but overall we hope you experience an improvement in both the visual and gameplay department. Our team has been working their tails off to bring this together and we’re proud of it. We hope you enjoy the Demo! - Mutant

[h3]FOLLOW US FOR MORE[/h3]
That’s it for this week. Be sure to share the game with your friends! Every little bit helps. 

As always, thanks for reading! Stay safe out there. <3 If you want to stay up to date with KAIJU FISHING, you can Wishlist the game on Steam, join our Discord or follow us on Twitter @MutantStudios.

Now on to the good stuff!

Demo Version 0.0.3.5.1 is now released. Here's yer patch notes:

General Gameplay
The telescope zoom feature has been disabled for now. We need to spend time stabilizing it for it to be less nauseating, so we're taking it out. It will return in the full release.

Controls
Mouse and Keyboard are now in the Demo!
For anyone on a previous Beta Branch, Mouse and Keyboard controls rebound in some places to adjust for Medium Fishing controls. Most should be the same, but pay attention to the tutorials to make sure!

Movement
Open Sail Movement
Speed increased from 15 to 35

Speed increased from 5 to 15

notes.title: YOUUUUU'RE OUT!!
notes.content:
Weekly Dev Update #38
Week of February 1, 2021

Aye, happy February! One month down, eleven to go. Time really flies.

We’re keeping our cards a bit closer to the vest in some senses because we do want to have some big surprises in the coming weeks. We've shared a little about our plans for the core gameplay stuff which included plans to update the demo, introduce medium fishing, and update some pretty big elements of the experience like the User Interface. 

[h3]Three Strikes and You’re Out![/h3]
What I [i]will[/i] preview now is a change-up planned for fishing that we’re testing now. 

Currently we’re testing a few changes coming down the road for fishing. We had a few things up our sleeves that didn’t make the feature list for the demo, so we’re testing them further now and will apply them if we feel they meet our goals. We've been getting a decent amount of feedback from our Demo so we're ready to start makin' new waves based on that.

First up, we’re adjusting tension and how fish moves affect it. Tension should be a fun mechanic to wrestle with, more about timing when you reel and when you let the line run a bit. It should be clear and easy to manage, but punishing if you try to bulldoze your way through it. Our first round of testing will increase tension on general reeling while lowering the build-up caused by fish attacks. This will increase how impactful your reeling is (which will also have base speed increased a bit to compensate) and create a larger difference in the pace of encounters between reeling and not. We'll include numbers and more specific changes as we lock em in.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/adb2bc814a400e79c0f1eb18f5a5e9fa500eab8f.gif[/img]

At the same time, the fish attacks need to feel more impactful in a way that doesn’t randomly spike tension and lead to confusion or frustration with line breaks. Our test for this will be a “three strikes” system, like baseball, as a baseline. You’ll get a set amount of strikes for each encounter, gaining a strike for each missed QTE. This emphasizes some QTEs as ‘damaging’ and others as positional and lets us add a sort of “health counter” for your line during each fight. This will allow us more flexibility in making some fish more aggressive and will increase clarity on when you miss QTEs and what the exact punishment is. You’ll also be able to increase how many strikes you have using the correct baits for each fish so you can improve your window for catching.

With these two main changes on the way, we’re confident we can improve the fishing experience in the demo and better set ourselves up for success in the main game. We’ll show off these changes in the next few weeks to give you a visual of what they’ll look like so stay tuned!

notes.title: CHONKY BUGS AND LONG TASKS
notes.content:
Weekly Dev Update #27
Week of October 19, 2020

This week at Mutant… we keep on the grind.

Last week, we had a lovely livestream on Steam for the Digital Tabletop Festival. We sat down with one of our programmers to play QUESTR - a game that he didn’t work on. If you haven’t heard of it, it’s a smaller game that twists RPG adventures with Tinder that we released all the way back in 2017.

From what we could tell, that stream had between 150 and 250 viewers (or people just browsing the store page) at any given time so if you were around thanks for hanging out! We really like these live Festival events that Steam has been doing so very much looking forward to more!

[h3]SEVERAL HOURS LATER...[/h3]
Some weeks I feel like I struggle to convey how much really gets done. Art stuff is easier to show progress or just show new assets… like this chonky boy. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/c74091bef492419d5c06af2a5c3c15601ee02682.png[/img]
As Simba would say, "Slimey... yet satisfying!"

But sometimes gameplay stuff is much more subtle or, worse for my typing of these, behind the scenes or hidden in a script.

The reality is that we’re really focused on nailing some of these key features so it takes time. So while it feels like we’ve been working on the same sort of features week after week, we are making steady progress! For example, medium fishing is a groundwork for so many features around different parts of the game, the time spent here will pay off later as we build out more content.

While launching his side career of live streaming old Mutant games on Steam, our talented programmer has been hard at work with medium fish. There’s been a lot of systems laying over each other to get medium fishing to a playable state. They had to path, move, react, attack, and play nice with our water assets… it’s taking a lot of math and technical skill and creativity to get this feature off the ground - or I guess, into the water? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/8a9ccd27d68c4e9090f1fe3260aa42c40101d4af.gif[/img]

With even just a simple clip like this, there's a lot going into it. We have our water asset, Crest, being highlighted in full spectacle. Crest has been a great tool, but it doesn't just do what you need with zero effort. We have to keep it updated and fitting with our physics and gameplay mechanics, so it takes work - not always pretty to show off. Then you have the rope tool, applying the weight of the fish, the speed, getting the tension... all that fun stuff that then doubles back onto the water physics. Then we have our pathing system for the fish to guide itself around - which has to apply force and work in it's own right.

All this before, really, any gameplay can be layered on top. So... it's a complicated thing that takes a lot of time and testing. We are aiming to have more to show by the end of the week, so hopefully an exciting update next Monday!

notes.title: THINKING WITH PORTALS
notes.content:
Weekly Dev Update #19
Week of August 24

This week at Mutant… we shifted some gears to talk about what the story means in Kaiju Fishing and how we can better use the environment to take advantage of the ultimate goal: catching and fighting big monsters and fish.

This will be a behind-the-development look at our story process and how Kaiju Fishing has changed and continues to evolve.

[h3]A BRIEF HISTORY[/h3]
From the beginning, Kaiju Fishing has always been a story about the environment. We drew on many monster movie concepts that basically boil down to: humans treated the Earth badly and now monsters either want to live here or they want to save the world from humans. From Godzilla to Pacific Rim to even some other inspirations for this game like Disney’s Moana. Something in the world is out of balance, your adventure is to face these monsters and restore the world.

The first draft waaay back at the start was a very bleak take on the world - honestly. If you look back to the Kickstarter we ran for this concept a year ago, it was much more akin to Shadow of the Colossus (even in name, Shadow of the Leviathan) and had a much darker tone overall. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/3f0ecdfe42f0f2cbd2f390a29dbd304cca504539.jpg[/img]
We’ve since abandoned that in favor of a lighter fishing adventure with more focus on fishing and less focus on brooding cinematics.

This new direction already opened the game up to being a more fun world. We laid out plans for fun characters, more wild concepts for fish (that could be slightly goofy too), and started fresh on a more vibrant art style. Runa got a pet, Skipper, and we got a lot of joy out of imagining the side characters that could populate the areas - like these round, lovable Seals. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/ddd8c338fe7ec7b7d9d95ed41a64cd9617934473.jpg[/img]
I still love them.

And before you get worried about their fate, they’ll still be involved. Promise.

From there, the next narrative pitch was a much more narrative-focused game - with a lot of nods and inspiration from Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker and Ocarina of Time. It was a direction that felt good to imagine because it was [i]epic.[/i] The world was lively and the adventure’s scale was huge. That was, in truth, probably always a bit ambitious for us. We're only four people and we’d like to finish this game sometime in the next year, not the next decade. Someday maybe we’ll make an art-book out of the original story and release it. For now, it will likely stay mostly a secret as we shifted once more. Some of it will become "legend" in the new context and will be treated as history of the world, which is kind of nice from a lore-writing perspective.

A moment of clarity helped us here after I re-watched Ponyo for the millionth time. That combined with listening to the first Pacific Rim music gave us a breakthrough.

[h3]THINKING WITH PORTALS[/h3]
The world of Kaiju Fishing in our minds has always been a magical place where spirits and mystery are plentiful. We wanted very much to elevate fishing into the “fantasy” category. The latest concept is a world where the past is flooded and these creatures roam through rifts/portals that are all around. The original concepts for the different villages will be there… but under the ocean.

We immediately jumped to this idea as a way to amplify fishing. We have always been chasing the question "How can we ramp up fishing to make it more epic and fantastic?" The first answer for us was obvious: make them bigger. Way bigger. Instead of reeling them in, they drag the boat. The next step is entirely about the context for where they come from and how we can push the limits on exploring for new fishing zones. 

And so we ended up discussing portals to another dimension, like Pacific Rim. The fish come and go through them, they can be hooked through them, and more portals can be discovered or opened through small puzzles around the world. This direction gives us a lot of freedom with the world to really open it up with new things to discover. It also provides us with a clear way to encourage discovery and visually show where your next fishing spot might be. Whatever we would lose in the "epic" narrative, we would gain even more in the gameplay. And we don't lose out on most of the key characters we want to bring to life. In fact, we think this new context gives them a lot of shared interests in the world.

So that's where we're at now. The scope feels better and we get to really dig into what makes fishing in Kaiju Fishing so fantastic and magical. 

[h3]DEMO UPDATES COMING SOON!?[/h3]
In the coming weeks, we want to push an update to the Demo of Kaiju Fishing that includes a lot. 
[list]
[*] We’ll be showcasing Medium sized fish for the first time, something we’re very excited about. These fish will test you with bigger attacks and more movement.
[*] Lots of bug-fixes and Quality of Life things.
[*] Our visuals will have received a decently big update.
[*] Crafting will be available in a small dose to create new baits.
[*] Mouse and Keyboard controls!
[*] And hopefully some narrative clues will find their way in.
[/list]
Now… with that deadline in mind you might be thinking ‘That’s right about when the next Steam Festival will be!’ And you’d be right... BUT! We won’t be applying to be featured in the October Festival. We’re hoping to make a big splash with our Demo updates even without the Festival’s featuring and we’ll need a lot of help to do that. We’ll be sharing more on social media with ways that you (yes, you!) can help us by streaming and sharing your experience with the game. We’ll also be looking to set up our own streaming times for you to come say hi to us too!

No, we want to push for an even bigger reveal and we won’t be quite there in a month. Steam announced recently that games can only be featured in Festivals once per year going forward so we want to pick our moment carefully. For the Spring Festival however...

Let’s just say, we’re very much looking forward to that opportunity.

Weekly Dev Update #17
Week of July 27

Hello all! Hope your August is off to a great start. It was a quiet week for us so I wanted to just quickly talk about a change in our process and give an update on our office situation.

[h3]GO ON, GIT![/h3]
Today’s as good a day as any to talk briefly about a transition in our process. We’ve been using Unity Collab as the primary method of sharing our project between multiple people on the team for quite a few projects now. It’s worked pretty well for smaller projects, but as Kaiju Fishing has grown so too has our need to share a larger project.

At the turn of the Summer Festival, Collab started giving us a fair amount of trouble. It caused more than its share of crashes and ultimately became a hindrance on the progress we could make. When this happened, we made the switch to Git. It took a bit for us to transition, but it will be worthwhile given how much time we’ll save in the long run.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/8826102203a63d1718b1a9924864b939ef71c486.png[/img]

[h3]HOW’S THE OFFICE?[/h3]
Speaking of a long run… Four months ago, Mutant Studios went into a work-from-home set-up. In the time since, barely anyone has set foot inside the office. This week, one of us bravely returned. To clean. The good news is that the office is exactly how we left it except with a thin layer of dust on basically everything.

To us, the pandemic has been a challenge to our processes and flow. We’re still working hard and communicating every step of the way, but it’s different. Weekly Dev Update #14
Week of July 6

It’s been a few weeks since our last update, but we’re back! Our progress the last few weeks was mostly focused on behind the scenes things on our end, so we figured we’d save the details for a singular update! Now we’re back and hitting the ground running.

[h3]THE FESTIVAL[/h3]
Let’s talk about the Steam Festival from a few weeks ago! Some technical hiccups aside for our streams, the Festival was a lot of fun. We played some demos, wishlisted a lot of other Indies, and gathered some feedback on our own demo!

If you played the Kaiju Fishing Demo, you’re our favorite kind of person <3 Thanks so much for trying the game. We have a lot of things we want to add, but we are always excited to share what we’re working on!

[h3]STEPPIN’ UP[/h3]
Part of our process post-Festival is updating our Unity project. Kaiju Fishing needed to be bumped up a few versions in order to fully implement our water asset (Crest) and add new effects and visuals. notes.title: FISHING PRIDE!
notes.content:
FISHING PRIDE!
Weekly Dev Update #13
Week of May 25

Hey. How are you? Doin okay? Same, same. We’re gettin’ by. Just doin’ game dev things. Meetings, artings, programmings, bug fixings… more meetings. The usual. Cool, cool. Should we talk about the game?

Let’s do it.

[h3]TANKS A LOT![/h3]Heh.. anyways.. That joke will make sense in a minute. Story-time.

There’s a certain element of pride that fishing brings. When I was a kid, I went fishing with my family at some tiny lake in California. There were a dozen groups gathered around this tiny lake area (before social distancing was a thing) and everyone had a couple of lines in the water. Nobody was really finding much luck. Families were out here maybe teaching their kids how to cast or whatever (hey, that was us!). And then, my little brother’s line suddenly shoots out and the rod bends at a harsh angle. Everyone looks over.  

The fight was on. For the next five minutes, we watched my brother (who was like 6 at the time) wrestle and reel this thing back and forth. It looked like the rod might snap in half. Other groups pulled their lines out of the water to make way as this fish twisted and dragged back and forth across the entire pond. All eyes on the one catch of the day. Everyone was rooting for this kid to land a fish because it was a spectacle.

And, mind you, my brother had never caught a fish ever. He was six. 

After five grueling minutes, he finally gets it close and we net it. The groups around clap and show their support. His first ever fish and it was quite the showing. (Oh wow that happened, eye roll right?) Well, it did. And he stood there with this big, dumb grin showing off his catch. That’s some pride.

My point is that we want to capture that emotion and what better way to show off your catches than letting you keep your favorite fish in your own personal fish tank! It’s still early in development, but this feature will let you show off your favorites and… there might even be ways to keep your bigger catches… We’ll save that for another day.

So as a teaser, here’s a quick look at the beginnings of the Fish Tank feature:[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/5a05c0bdb6e3e8bab16ea87ac06fd8ef185e9615.png[/img]

In the demo, you’ll be able to save just one of each type of fish to view later but we plan to heavily expand this feature later! We also want to give you a chance to really cheese with your catch by posing next to your accomplishments. More later.

[h3]STEAM FESTIVAL AROUND THE CORNER[/h3]The Steam Festival is around the corner and we are still thrilled to be a part of it. We’re excited to show off our work and we’re excited to see all the other Indie games in the event!

We’ll be announcing our official schedule next week for the Dev Live Streams, Dev Talks, and more but I’ll leave this briefly overview of our general plans:
[list]
[*] Gameplay Live Stream on the 9th. Watch us catch some fish and hang out.
[*] Discord Hang-Outs every day of the week in the mornings.
[*] Plus we’ll be watching Steam Discussions to respond when we can and continuing to share cool stuff on our Twitter (@MutantStudios). 
[/list]

The official times will be posted next week and be live on the Kaiju Fishing Demo Store Page during the Event, so hopefully we’ll see you there! It’s promising to be a fun week!

[h3]FOLLOW US FOR MORE[/h3]That's all for now. We hope you're enjoying our weekly updates. Be sure to share them with your friends to get the word out about KAIJU FISHING. As always, thanks for reading! Stay safe out there. <3

BACK TO SCHOOLS (OF FISH)
Weekly Dev Update #12
Week of May 18

This week was sort of a blur. All the days in quarantine sort of blend together. (Anyone else or is that just us?) We met at the start of this week to take a look at our Demo and talk about what comes next. We have plenty to do so we dove right in. 

[h3]ALWAYS A BIGGER FISH[/h3]So I wanted to take this week to talk briefly about this line we’re trying to walk. Kaiju Fishing is a fantasy adventure game with fishing as a core mechanic. What this means is that we need a fun, engaging fishing experience that we can expand on as players progress but also one that doesn’t force an overly deep understanding of fishing as it would be in real life.

Our goal is to create a fishing game that escalates to the scale of epic monsters and still lands for players who want to enjoy just fishing in each zone. So this first demo is focused on the small fry, but it’s laying the groundwork for larger fish.

[h3]THE ECOSYSTEM... LIVES[/h3]One of the first things we want to establish is how you interact with the world and see it. We have a beautiful ocean system and going forward we’re looking for even more ways to take advantage of being able to see under the water. 

So we’re going to be showing off our next key part of the fishing equation: schools of fish![img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/6eb19936899cb20b083085835b9863885fa07f12.gif[/img]

There’s plenty more to do with showing our environments and evolving the way the player can interact with them, but we think this is a cool start! There are more surprises to be found in these systems, but we’ve save those for later…

[h2]BEHIND THE SCENES[/h2]This week, we’re working on the hidden stuff. It’s not pretty looking (yet) but we’ve made good progress on getting our menus functioning and all the settings linked up to the rest. Once we have art for those menus we’ll share them with you here. 

The boat looks great (thanks to our artist, Sarah!) and the characters are up next! As we settled from the wake of the boat (heh), Sarah made some smaller but cool assets to add to our world.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/b53645f95e8bddbdb0f1dc58d5edf541375932df.jpg[/img]

[h2]FOLLOW US FOR MORE[/h2]Bit of a lighter week for this update, but just know that we’re still working on stuff. Thanks for reading! Stay safe out there. <3

notes.content:
[h2]KAIJU FISHING Dev Update #2: Fish AI and Boat Textures![/h2]Week of March 9

Hey all! Another week, another update. We spent the majority of this week just tuning up fishing for small fish, with some passes on input feedback and updates to the fish AI. 

[h3]THEY’RE… ALIVE![/h3]Our talented gameplay programmer set up a sweet little system for building fish which lets us essentially build “move sets” for each fish. We have some core attacks for the fish to do, but each one is unique in which moves they’ll favor and how they chain their moves together. It’s a simple but robust set-up that will give us a lot of freedom to give each fish type their own personality!

This feature is the core of our game so we really, really need to nail it. So far, we’re pleased with the direction but it needs a little more love! We'll be giving it another pass for game-feel and updating the art in the coming weeks.

[h3]WE NEED(ED) A BIGGER BOAT[/h3]And we got one! This is the fourth design iteration on our boat since the early stages of development latest and it’s been a worthwhile process! We're still polishing up some of the details but we couldn't wait to get it moving! Here’s the boat roamin' around!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/63c7c0de1cb848a50da8b0188fdec693e16de6f9.png[/img]

We also worked on updating the general movement and third-person-camera - more tuning to be done next week.

[h3]FOLLOW US FOR MORE[/h3]Those are the main two things we worked on this week. Sort of a short update for this week, but know that we’re working’ away. A lot of the features in development right now are core pillars and once we have them in a good spot, we can build a lot of content around them fairly quickly! 

Thanks for reading! <3

notes.content:
[h2]KAIJU FISHING Dev Update #1: Small Fishing[/h2] Hey all! Welcome to the first Development Update! These updates will give you a taste of what we're working on during the week and keep you up to date on major features as we work. 

Fishing is one of the core pillars in our game so we want to make sure it feels good - starting from our smallest fish and working to our literal monsters. This first development update showcases a couple of things, including our in-progress boat design with a bending fishing rod as well as some new animations we're testing.

Our fish will be set up to wriggle around using Tail Animator, a sweet little tool from the Unity Asset Store. The ocean is Crest, a robust asset that includes a TON of features that we plan to take full advantage of.

[h3]CASTING[/h3] New casting animation and targeting! 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/92872b4a24d7617f304fb9f44389a5bba26c4e3a.gif[/img]

[h3]TENSION[/h3] When your tension is getting too high, the rod bend will be extreme and the line will turn red. Make sure you let up on reeling so you don't snap your line!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36885541/7ee468231562cd8fc5d6f2d3004581ecd19ff2ae.gif[/img]

[h3]MORE SOON![/h3] There's still more work and polish to do on fishing, including more VFX and UI, but we're pleased with the progress so we thought we'd share. Look for more soon! We're going to aim to do little updates like this once a week until we launch, so Wishlist or Follow to check in on us!

[h2]FOLLOW US![/h2]
For other smaller updates and fun, check us out on [url=https://twitter.com/MutantStudios]Twitter @MutantStudios[/url] or on our [url=http://discord.gg/Meuq8ea]Discord[/url]!
